name: Immigration & Checkpoints Authority

scam_info.sample: Scam variant #1: Calls from scammers impersonating ICA officers ... The calls would then be transferred to another scammer impersonating a China official.
scam_info.notes: Joint SPF-ICA advisory issued 25 Sep 2026 (page "Last updated 18 Oct 2026"), with two variants. Mirrors SPF news 20260925_advisory_on_scams_involving_the_immigration_checkpoints_authority_ica.

scam_info.sample: scammers impersonate ICA officers through phone or video calls. To appear legitimate, they may use the ICA crest as a profile picture, or wear attire resembling ICA’s uniforms during video calls.
scam_info.notes: Issued 10 June 2026. Lists what an ICA caller will never do. The only phone given is the official verification line (call agents 6391 6100).

scam_info.sample: ICA was alerted to a fake letter and tax invoice that were received by a member of the public bearing the ICA letterhead and a signature of an officer allegedly from the ICA.
scam_info.notes: Issued 28 Mar 2026. PR-application agent fraud (fee close to $5,000). Names no entity.

scam_info.sample: Usually originated from spoofed ICA numbers and unknown numbers, which might or might not contain the “+” prefix.
scam_info.notes: Issued 05 Jul 2024: about 500 scam-call cases in Apr-Jun 2024.

scam_info.sample: (issued 28 July 2023) scam calls impersonating ICA officers; page cites official helplines 1800-255-0000 and 1800-722-6688
members of the public have been receiving calls from “+65 6812 5555”, which is similar to our SafeTravel Enquiries Helpline “6812 5555”.
scam_info.notes: Issued 13 Aug 2021. Spoofed caller ID = an official ICA number. This is a caller-ID-spoofing indicator, not a scam-owned line.

scam_info.sample: there is a fake ICA website [ica-mom.online] that looks identical to the official ICA website [www.ica.gov.sg].
members of the public have been receiving calls from different numbers, such as the Immigration Offender hotline “1800 3916150”
(issued 8 August 2019) Public Advisory On Scam Letters From ICA
On 25 June 2019, a member of public received a call from the Immigration & Checkpoints Authority (ICA)’s Call Centre number “6391 6100”.
The official ICA website is https://www.ica.gov.sg/ and all of ICA’s official e-Services can be found on the Information and e-Services page .
scam_info.notes: Last updated 20 Oct 2026. General guidance; lists no domains. Official ICA website and e-Service URLs contain ".ica.gov.sg". Reports go to the anti-scam helpline 1800 722 6688 or i-witness.

Sitemap (from robots.txt; 1,484 URLs; no lastmod) lists 709 media-room URLs. 12 match scam/fake/impersonat/phish/misleading. Public-advisories listing shows "1-12 of 80 Listings" (latest 19 Aug 2026, MyICA Mobile Application). No RSS. Issue dates are in the page footer ("IMMIGRATION & CHECKPOINTS AUTHORITY <date>"); the "Last updated 18 Oct 2026" header is a bulk re-save date, not the issue date.

hotlines: 6391 6100 (ICA call centre; use to verify ICA calls)
apps: MyICA Mobile app (official; SGAC can be submitted via MyICA or the SGAC e-Service)

notes: Concrete indicators: fake site ica-mom.online (2021); spoofed ICA numbers. The SG Arrival Card annex of 63 paid/fake SGAC sites is under ica.gov.sg#sg-arrival-card. Hosts seen in page links: eservices.ica.gov.sg (/sgarrivalcard, /ecert), webchat.vica.gov.sg (VICA virtual assistant chat). api-vica-bp.vica.gov.sg was also referenced and not visited. ICA was among the 7 Home Team agencies in the MHA advisory of 12 Aug 2026 on >500 fake look-alike sites. SPF brand tags include "Immigration & Checkpoints Authority of Singapore (ICA)" (2 advisories).
